economy.summary: His campaign platform says government regulation and hyper-involvement are primary obstacles to small business success, and blames regulations, permit delays, and burdensome taxes for Pennsylvania losing residents to states with stronger economies.
economy.short: Says regulations, permit delays, burdensome taxes drive residents from Pennsylvania.

taxes.summary: Voted against the 2026-27 state budget, joining a York County House Republican statement saying the $50.85 billion plan spends roughly $3.65 billion more than projected revenues, relies on accounting maneuvers to defer costs, and burdens future taxpayers.
taxes.short: Voted no on 2026-27 budget, saying it overspends and defers costs.

abortion.summary: Sponsored 2023 legislation to prohibit abortion after fetal cardiac activity is detected, and his campaign website stated, 'I have a dream that Pennsylvania will someday outlaw abortion.' In a 2024 voter guide he supported prohibiting abortion except when necessary to save the mother's life.
abortion.short: Sponsored fetal-heartbeat abortion ban; says he hopes Pennsylvania outlaws abortion.

education.summary: His campaign platform supports parents' choice to enroll their children in public, private, charter, cyber, or home schools without government obstacles.
education.short: Supports parental choice among public, private, charter, cyber, homeschool options.

healthcare.summary: His official legislative site says his second-term priorities include pharmacy benefit manager reform, along with cutting regulations he calls burdensome; the site does not detail a broader healthcare platform.
healthcare.short: Names pharmacy benefit manager reform a second-term legislative priority.

energy.summary: His campaign platform criticizes state executive agencies, including the Department of Environmental Protection, for what he calls burdensome regulations, delays, and fees on business owners, farmers, and homeowners; it does not state a broader energy policy.
energy.short: Criticizes DEP regulations as burdensome; states no broader energy policy.

guns.summary: His campaign platform opposes adding taxes, regulations, and other requirements on gun owners, and says he supports prosecuting violent criminals and cracking down on illegal immigration.
guns.short: Opposes new taxes and regulations on gun owners; supports prosecuting violent criminals.

taxes.summary: His campaign website describes his approach as mixing fiscally conservative and socially progressive views, saying there is strength in a moderate view that sets reasonable limits on government, including limits on taxation; it does not state specific tax proposals.
taxes.short: Describes himself as fiscally conservative; favors limits on taxation.

abortion.summary: In a candidate survey response he said he supports legislation that would firmly establish every woman's access to the full spectrum of reproductive healthcare, and he opposes mandatory waiting periods and counseling requirements, citing their impact on low-income women.
abortion.short: Supports legislation establishing access to full spectrum of reproductive healthcare.

education.summary: His campaign platform says quality public education at the K-12 level is vital to maintaining the state's overall competitive position.
education.short: Says quality public K-12 education vital to state's competitive position.

healthcare.summary: His campaign platform says access to quality, affordable healthcare is needed by everyone and that Pennsylvania needs to maintain high-quality medical schools to help recruit the next generation of healthcare professionals.
healthcare.short: Says everyone needs affordable healthcare; supports maintaining medical schools.

energy.summary: His campaign platform says clean air and clean water, reduced sprawl, and efficient recycling and waste reduction are key to maintaining livable communities.
energy.short: Says clean air, water, recycling, reduced sprawl keep communities livable.
